source.title: Emergence of Invariance and Disentanglement in Deep Representations

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some plotted values are described in text but not numerically reported.
record.tranche_reason: Tests generalization and overfitting under an information-based regularizer, and examines how model width relates to test error using different measures and training settings from the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017) for standard CNNs fitting random labels; that cited result is not a row. Rows below cover the paper's own random-label regularization experiment, test-error plots, and representation information measurements. The cluttered-MNIST invariance results do not measure the training-test gap and are not rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 and Section 7.1 bear on V1 in a new, explicitly information-regularized setting: Small AlexNet can fit random labels at low β, while natural-label training yields held-out accuracy above the random-label result. The width experiment does not establish that its sweep is beyond the width required for zero training error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors principally conclude that reducing information in the weights promotes minimal, invariant and disentangled representations under their assumptions. Their experiments also verify a predicted random-label fitting transition and show that increasing parameter count alone makes All-CNN test error plateau.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an information bottleneck regularizer and multiplicative weight noise for the random-label experiment; the width sweep uses weight decay. It does not reproduce the unregularized recipes or the specific settings in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The β value changes whether random-label models overfit or underfit and changes test error in the All-CNN bias-variance experiment. Increasing model width makes test error plateau in the reported CIFAR-10 sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: All-CNN test error falls and then plateaus as filter counts increase under weight decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing convolutional-network width can preserve good test performance under weight decay, without a demonstrated post-interpolation regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Varying information regularization produces an underfitting-to-overfitting test-error curve.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information retained in the weights provides a controllable complexity measure associated with held-out performance.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Machine Learning Research 18 (2018), as stated in the paper text; venue metadata provided with the record says Information Theory and Applications Workshop.
record.problems: The main random-label results and the width sweep are shown in plots without numerical values in the text. The real-label and random-label findings use different training settings, so they do not establish coexistence under the same standard, unregularized recipe. The nuisance-information estimate is described as having no guarantees on approximation quality, but it does not measure the mapped generalization-gap versions.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the paper's stated information-in-weights versus label-corruption plot (Figure 2 right): it measures information needed to fit labels, not test error or the training-test gap named by the versions. No row for cluttered-MNIST nuisance invariance (Figure 4): it measures I(z;n), not the mapped generalization outcomes. Figure 1's natural-label accuracy result is recorded as R6; precise plotted values were not extracted.

untested.parts: Coexistence without explicit regularization; the original architecture and dataset coverage; natural-label generalization for the All-CNN and ResNet random-label experiments. Exact chance-level random-label test accuracy cannot be recovered from the supplied Figure 1 rendering.
Whether widening beyond the width required for zero training error continues lowering test error; the specified unregularized one-hidden-layer networks and datasets.
All parts: no convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
All parts: no suitably controlled dropout versus no-dropout test-error comparison.
All parts: no empirical ranking of generalization gaps by magnitude-aware sharpness.
All parts: no removal of memorized examples and retraining.

missing.what: Small AlexNet random-label held-out accuracy across β and training-set size. The caption describes uniformly low test accuracy, but the record contains only random-label training error and natural-label test accuracy. Record readable values and a chance baseline if available.

record.verdict_notes: Strong information regularization preventing memorization does not challenge V1's unregularized claim. The theoretical Hessian–information connection does not test V7's empirical correlation or ranking claim. No exact plotted values were reconstructed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the same unregularized training recipe on random and natural labels; its random-label experiment explicitly uses an information regularizer, and the natural-label experiment uses weight decay or the information-regularized loss.
Does not test one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained to zero training error on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10, or a sweep specifically past the width required for zero error.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on image test error.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD.
No large-batch versus small-batch generalization comparison.
No experiment adding or removing dropout as an intervention.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare sharpness with other gap measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and retrain.

rows.subject: All-CNN
rows.size_stated: number of weights varied; exact values not stated in text
rows.operation_detail: Increased the number of filters across layers and measured test error.
rows.note: The paper states test error plateaus as the number of weights increases rather than increasing. Exact points are only plotted.
rows.check: Relink away from V1. The experiment measures width versus test error, but reports neither training error nor the interpolation threshold needed to determine V2's post-fitting effect. Its plateau is not evidence that V2 fails in its stated regime.

rows.subject: All-CNN
rows.operation_detail: Varied β in the information bottleneck loss and measured test error.

conditions.value: varied; values not stated in text

rows.note: The authors describe a bias-variance curve: low information tends to underfit, while too much information tends to overfit. No numeric test-error values are stated.
rows.check: Test error versus information regularization does not measure coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization, or any other listed version.

rows.subject: Small AlexNet
rows.size_stated: small version; exact structure in Table 1
rows.operation_detail: Varied β while training on natural CIFAR-10 labels; test accuracy shown in Figure 1.
rows.note: The paper says accuracy increases with the number of training samples and is higher near β = 1 for real labels. This is not the same unregularized recipe as the random-label experiment; exact values and full setup are not stated here.
rows.check: Natural-label test accuracy supplies one component of V1; it is not a complete coexistence measurement. Figure 1 jointly presents natural- and random-label outcomes across β and sample size, so the record's assertion that these necessarily use different recipes is unsupported. The recipe is explicitly regularized.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V1 from this row alone. Natural-label test accuracy increases with sample count and is higher near β = 1; establishing coexistence additionally requires random-label fitting and held-out performance.
source_check.problem: A natural-label generalization component alone does not demonstrate a partial coexistence effect.

relation.reason: Figures 1 and 2 report the study's own random-label fitting and natural-label generalization results.

tranche.reason: The experiments address the same random-label memorization and natural-label generalization question on CIFAR-10 with overlapping architectures, using a different method: explicit information-bottleneck regularization and stochastic weights.

source_check.notes: Figure 1's surface uses interpolation and inpainting; exact accuracy values and an explicit numerical chance comparison are not stated. The supplied text is the 2018 revision/publication of the 2017 arXiv study.

reader_labels.reason: All three architectures show the reported transition from fitting to underfitting as β changes, but this tests an explicit information regularizer rather than the version's shared standard, unregularized recipe (R1–R3). The paper also reports natural-label test accuracy only in a separate regularized setting (R6).
